gen-fs-bevellier-gf-faustina: Bevellier packs stencil-cut strokes of one weight into close, high lowercase, with no stress in the curves. Faustina stays easy through a column, stems only a shade heavier.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-pridi: Proud small letters in Pridi stand almost capital-sized, with generous gaps where curves meet the stems. Under Bevellier, those serif letters keep a column moving without sharp thins.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-scope-one: Stencil-cut one-weight strokes huddle close in Bevellier, squat, high, and graceful. And Scope One keeps a traditional serif column going, counters spilling out beside stubby extenders.
gen-fs-bonny-gf-lexend-giga: Gaping literary curves packed into tight lines announce Bonny at once. Lexend Giga walks a stretch of copy in flat, widely tracked sans, ascenders barely clearing the line.
gen-fs-bonny-gf-lexend-mega: Lexend Mega shows a one-nib skeleton and nearly cap-high bodies throughout each word. Bonny brings a milder inscription-like weight under a stretch of that monoweight sans-serif copy.
gen-fs-bonny-gf-lexend-tera: A plotter-pen line in Lexend Tera leaves open-faced curves standing as far apart as stepping stones. Under Bonny, that sans-serif stays easy across a whole column.
gen-fs-erode-gf-julius-sans-one: Julius Sans One spreads letters with open-ended curves and almost matching capital and lowercase. And Erode keeps slightly thinner hairlines above a stretch of that plain sans copy.
gen-fs-erode-gf-lexend-tera: Single-thread unshaded linework reads contemporary and clean, each rounded letter left open-faced and far apart. Lexend Tera holds a stretch of copy while Erode keeps gentler modulation above.
gen-irish-grover-gf-sintony: Fun is the first hit of Irish Grover, organic and a bit wild. Sintony keeps a stretch of sans-serif copy smooth, with a chunky midzone and no clogged curves.
gen-fs-expose-gf-glegoo: Glegoo offers a serif with big counters and wide, unclosed mouths in the small letters, refined and editorial. Under Expose, that serif holds a column without fuss.
gen-fs-expose-gf-piazzolla: Compressed, almost cap-high letters pack Expose into a striking, refined line with very little pause. Piazzolla holds a column as a text serif, e like a pried clasp.
gen-fs-expose-gf-scope-one: Almost no gap between x-height and caps marks Expose. Scope One keeps a traditional serif column going, counters spilling out beside stubby extenders and a big x-height.
gen-fs-gambarino-gf-lexend-zetta: Lexend Zetta spreads widely tracked cut-ribbon strokes and high-bodied small letters, contemporary in feel. And Gambarino floods stems with ink and hairline whiskers, dramatic above that line.
gen-fs-kalam-archivo: Hand-drawn lines packed tight announce Kalam right from the first word. Archivo keeps a stretch of sans-serif copy moving, curves opening outward under a commanding x-height.
gen-fs-kalam-clash-grotesk: Kalam bunches inviting, cozy handwritten lines into a tight bundle. Clash Grotesk holds a wire-bent sans through a stretch, easier in brief doses than a marathon.
